articles.title: French actor Gerard Depardieu to stand trial on  2018 rape charge: Lawyer
articles.summary: French actor Gerard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial on a charge of raping an actress at his Paris home in 2018, one of his lawyers told The
articles.body: French actor Gerard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial on a charge of raping an actress at his Paris home in 2018, one of his lawyers told The Associated Press on Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate case.Defense lawyer Delphine Meillet wrote in a message to the AP that the 77-year-old actor would face trial over only one of the two alleged rapes reported by actress Charlotte Arnould.Depardieu, who has denied the rape allegations, had challenged an investigating judge's August 2025 decision to send him to trial.The Paris Court of Appeal upheld that decision Thursday in relation to one of the two alleged rapes."He disputes the decision," Meillet told AP, without specifying whether Depardieu would file a further appeal.Arnould first lodged a complaint in 2018, when she was 22. The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.A French cinema icon faces a #MeToo reckoningFor half a century, Depardieu was a towering figure in French cinema.With his hulking frame, crooked nose and commanding screen presence, he became one of the country's most recognizable cultural exports, earning an Oscar nomination for "Cyrano de Bergerac" and a Golden Globe for "Green Card."But accusations of sexual misconduct and his subsequent conviction have increasingly overshadowed his cinematic legacy.Earlier this month, Depardieu dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set in 2021, accepting an 18-month suspended prison sentence and issuing a public apology."I was found guilty," Depardieu said in a written statement on Nov. 16, adding that he accepted the sentence."I therefore offer my deep and sincere apologies to those who may have suffered," he said.Depardieu was convicted in May 2025 of groping a set decorator and an assistant during the filming of "Les Volets Verts" ("The Green Shutters"). The case was widely seen as a test of the French film industry's response to the #MeToo movement."On film sets, I have long hidden behind provocation and crude humor. I believed my words and some of my actions had no consequences. But they did, particularly coming from someone who held as much power as I once did," Depardieu said in his statement.Accusations against Depardieu sparked a national debateDepardieu's behavior toward women came under renewed scrutiny in December 2023 after a television documentary showed him repeatedly making obscene remarks and gestures during a 2018 trip to North Korea.French President Emmanuel Macron drew criticism from women's rights activists at the time when he defended Depardieu, saying the actor "makes France proud."Macron invoked the presumption of innocence and said he would not participate in a "manhunt."The controversy exposed divisions in France over the #MeToo movement.In 2018, actress Catherine Deneuve and 99 other women signed an open letter defending men's freedom to pursue women and warning against what they saw as the movement's excesses.Born in 1948 into a working-class family in the central French city of Chateauroux, Depardieu overcame a speech impediment to become one of France's most prolific actors.His career spanned hundreds of films, including "The Last Metro," "Jean de Florette" and the popular "Asterix" franchise.His excesses off-screen also made international headlines, notably when he accepted a Russian passport from President Vladimir Putin in 2013 amid a dispute over French taxes.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Melissa Gilbert Expresses “Undying Gratitude” After Timothy Busfield’s Child Sex Abuse Case Dismissed
articles.summary: "This Thanksgiving I’m incredibly grateful for all those who came running toward us this year," she wrote in a lengthy Instagram post.
articles.body:
Melissa Gilbert took to her Instagram on Thanksgiving to express her "undying gratitude" after husband Timothy Busfield's child sex abuse case was dismissed .

"This Thanksgiving I'm incredibly grateful for all those who came running toward us this year," she wrote. "To those who checked in, took care of our home and animals when we were away, came to hearings, fed us, housed us, spoke up, testified, wrote letters, listened, comforted us, held our hands and checked in regularly, we love you."

"Our undying gratitude also, to our extraordinary team who bravely fought and continue to fight for so hard for what is right and true. On this day, as we all acknowledge the blessings in our lives, we send our love and eternal gratitude to each and every one of you," Gilbert added, who has been married to Busfield since 2013.

Last month, a judge overseeing the proceedings tossed out Busfield's case in Albuquerque, New Mexico, accusing prosecutors of failing to "act in a fair and impartial manner" and of violating grand jury statutes that are "designed to protect the structural integrity of our grand jury system."

He had been accused of child sex abuse on the set of the former Fox/Warner Bros. Television series The Cleaning Lady , episodes of which he directed between 2022 and 2024.

Throughout the proceedings, Gilbert defended Busfield , who denied the allegations. She told ABC's George Stephanopoulos in April 2026, "For Tim, it's done. He's canceled. Even if he's exonerated, he will always be that guy, the last person in the world who would hurt a child. And believe me, if I thought for a second that Tim Busfield hurt a child, he'd have a lot more to worry about than prison."

articles.title: Music at Oxford launches first mini South Asian culture festival
articles.summary: Your guide to a weekend of events at an "authentic South Asian experience" in Oxford.
articles.body:
A music charity is staging its first "mini festival" celebrating South Asian culture.

Music at Oxford kicks off in the city later and will feature tabla playing, dance workshops, music from the Sufi tradition and an Indian film screening.

Artistic and executive director, Rebecca Dawson, said the short weekend-long festival format gave people a chance to learn more about the culture at venues including the Sheldonian Theatre.

Dawson said all the concerts would have special decoration, lighting and amplification to make for "a really, really authentic South Asian experience".

Ssarod virtuoso Soumik Datta and his band will opening the event on Friday at the Sheldonian, with the final concert in their UK tour, Melodies in Slow Motion.

Saturday will feature a workshop and performance by UK-based tabla maestro Shahbaz Hussain , Bollywood and Gujarati dancing with Pooja Rajguru and a family-friendly rave with DJ Indy at the St Clement's Centre.

Singer Chahat Mahmood Ali Qawwal and his musicians will play music from the Sufi tradition at St Mary Magdalen.

On Sunday, researcher, writer and dancer Dr Ranjini Nair will give a talk at the Asian Cultural Centre.

The Jacqueline du Pré Music Building at St Hilda's College will host a screening of 2010 film Natarang and a "diverse fusion of Indian classical music and jazz" by Tabla For Two.

Dawson said some of the group's musicians had been University of Oxford students.

Trina Banerjee, who will be performing with the group, said she was "super excited, honoured and privileged to be a part of the festival".

Dawson said there was "a real thirst" for South Asian music locally: "We did three concerts previously ... and they were just so popular."

She said she found South Asian music "really virtuosic" and "exciting".

"I remember at the end of one concert last year, the musicians just played faster and faster - it was just incredible to watch how they did it," she said.

"We are moving now to a business model where we're going to do more mini festivals, looking at all kinds of different music around the world."

Recently, the filmmaker spoke about the changing audience preferences towards big-budget pan-India films, recalling how he had anticipated a shift in audience interest towards such projects two years ago.Allu Aravind talks predicting the trendDuring a press meet in Hyderabad on Thursday, a reporter pointed out that several top Telugu stars are currently focusing on ambitious pan-India films. However, audiences have reportedly started showing interest in films that are more classy and pleasant to watch as quoted by Hindustan Times.Responding to the observation, Allu Aravind smiled and said, “Any good businessman can imagine what is happening after two to three years. Take my answer as me predicting what would happen two years ago, too.”Allu Aravind talks about commercial cinemaAllu Aravind also stated that his comments should not be seen as a prediction that commercial films would lose their appeal. He said he continues to believe in commercial cinema and is also working towards making such films.“I have said this to anybody in general. This is not to say that two years back I predicted that so-called commercial cinema would see lower reception. It is also my effort to make commercial films. I don’t know if my future films will be the way you described. But in 2027 and 2028, I will be backing films with a huge star cast that will become blockbusters.”During the interaction, the reporter also asked whether he had shared the prediction with Allu Arjun. He then laughed and replied, “Not really.”Allu Arjun’s upcoming filmAllu Arjun was last seen in the 2024 blockbuster pan-India film ‘Pushpa 2: The Rule’ directed by Sukumar. The film went on to make over Rs. 1,742.10 crore worldwide. Now, he is working on his next big budget sci-fi project ‘Raaka’ with director Atlee.He also has a tentatively titled ‘AA23’ with filmmaker Lokesh Kanagaraj in the pipeline.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: How woke Hollywood is remaking, and ruining, every film you've ever loved
articles.summary: Hollywood's remake wave spans James Bond, a new "Harry Potter" series and Greta Gerwig's "Narnia," as Steven Spielberg warns IP will run out of gas.
articles.body: The watchword for Hollywood these days isn’t "blockbuster" or even "star." It’s IP, or intellectual property. Left Coast moviemakers are overwhelming their audiences with regurgitated plots, characters and titles. It’s like a global sense of déjà vu, only we all know we have done it before. Think I’m joking? We just saw Robert Pattinson named the seventh movie star James Bond (not counting the original "Casino Royale"). And HBO is working on a new "Harry Potter" series that’s scheduled to premiere on Christmas Day, just 15 years after we were done with the eight movies that made up the Daniel Radcliffe/Emma Watson era of "Potter." The left hates author J.K. Rowling, but it sure is eager to remake her classics. It’s too early to tell how woke "Potter" will be, though producers have already created a furor by race-swapping the character Severus Snape in what one outlet said generated "months of 'woke' casting backlash." And given the original cast’s rejection of all things Rowling, I fear they will modify more to spite her and make news. REACTIONS POUR IN AFTER HBO DROPS NEW TRAILER FOR ITS UPCOMING HARRY POTTER MEGA-SERIES Sadly, that remake is hardly alone. The "Chronicles of Narnia" movies are also being remade, with Greta Gerwig’s new version, "Narnia: The Magician's Nephew," due out in February, about 17 years after the last movie debuted. It has already gotten bad reviews for casting Meryl Streep as the voice of the lion Aslan, who is supposed to be male because he’s also a Christ figure. And Hollywood is hard at work redoing the classic Hitchcock horror flick, "The Birds," of course, changing the gender of the male lead to a movie "led by a new female protagonist," according to Deadline — with a far inferior director trying to outdo Hitchcock. DIRECTOR OF NEW ‘NARNIA’ MOVIE TAKES HEAT OVER CASTING OF MERYL STREEP AS CHRIST-LIKE LION ASLAN It’s all the intersection of greedy Hollywood and woke Hollywood. Greedy Hollywood will keep grinding out garbage because studios own the intellectual property. And woke Hollywood will keep making good shows and movies worse, deliberately disappointing more and more fandoms. Picture the three horrifying seasons of "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" done to every good movie and TV show you’ve ever loved. In 2025, nine of the top 10 movies at the box office were either sequels or remakes, in some way trading on existing IP. In 2026, we’ve had a few more movies break through, but remakes and sequels still make up more than half the top 10. How long before they redo "Band of Brothers," with diverse casting, of course? ETHAN HAWKE BLASTS HOLLYWOOD'S 'GREEDY BASTARDS,' PREDICTS MASSIVE REBELLION AGAINST POWERFUL ELITES Yes, this isn’t new. Even the controversial silent film "The Birth of a Nation" had a sequel more than 100 years ago. The 1970s ushered in sequels for one of the most critically acclaimed movies of all time — "The Godfather." And that was followed by a tidal wave of science fiction film franchises like "Star Trek" and "Star Wars." What we’re seeing now is different. It’s this endless cycle of books and graphic novels spawning movies, which in turn spawn TV shows, and perhaps new movies. The Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) shows how far off the rails this strategy can go. The original series had 23 movies, though many fans stopped with No. 22, 2019’s "Avengers: Endgame." 'THE MANDALORIAN AND GROGU' COLLAPSES IN SECOND WEEKEND AT BOX OFFICE, CEMENTING HUGE LOSS FOR DISNEY Disney didn’t stop there. Add 15 movies since then and 18 total series spanning 22 seasons, and you have a viewing public that doesn’t have a clue what is going on. But Disney didn’t like how poorly its recent woke movies were doing, so it is bringing back the very stars who made it all work. It’s even changing the ending of that entire series with an encore version of "Endgame." Meanwhile, you practically need AI just to watch it all and update you on the side plots. Hollywood producers are counting on each new release finding new fans and keeping some existing ones. That also means new merchandise, new spinoffs and more. Everything in the world becomes the MCU. Every beloved movie, TV show or book from your youth will now be executed (that’s the appropriate word) by someone with far less talent, style or skill. And, of course, with a far inferior cast. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION It’s a crisis so profound that famed director Steven Spielberg warned, "If all we make is known, branded IP, we’re going to run out of gas." He added: "There is nothing more important than giving the audience visual stories, and they can be in any form, but we need to tell more original stories." Clearly, nobody in Hollywood is listening to him. articles.title: Justin Timberlake Was ‘Really Reluctant’ to Make Tell-All Documentary: ‘I’ve Gone Through a Lot in the Last Five Years’
articles.summary: Justin Timberlake is opening up about his decision to participate in an upcoming tell-all documentary, saying he was initially “really reluctant.” As Variety...
articles.body:
Justin Timberlake is opening up about his decision to participate in an upcoming tell-all documentary, saying he was initially "really reluctant."

As Variety first reported , the singer is the subject of "Timberlake," a four-part documentary from director Fisher Stevens that will premiere on Apple TV Dec. 11. During an appearance on longtime friend Jimmy Fallon's late-night show on Thursday, Timberlake spoke for the first time about the doc, which sources told Variety delves into the infamous wardrobe malfunction with Janet Jackson and his relationship with Britney Spears.

"I was really reluctant to do it … I think I'm sort of famously private," Timberlake told Fallon. "I have a relationship with Fisher Stevens, who is a wonderful director and a great human. When Fisher first approached me to do this, I was reluctant, because I was like, 'I don't wanna talk about myself,' you know? But the more we sat down and talked, the more I found myself kind of searching for something that was beneath the surface a little more."

Timberlake said that once he eventually agreed, "I sort of mustered up some courage to talk about things that I've never talked about before. Things that even those that are closest to me don't know."

He added, "You just never know what somebody's going through, right? And I think I kind of decided, maybe people see my life from the outside and it's like, 'Wow!' But everybody's going through something, and I think I've gone through a lot in the last five years that I feel like has made me a better human and a better father, a better husband, a better friend."

Though Timberlake didn't detail the documentary's revelations, he has kept a relatively low-profile since his "Forget Tomorrow" world tour, which concluded last year. During the tour, he announced that he had been recently diagnose with Lyme disease, which had affected his performances. In 2024, he was also arrested for driving while intoxicated in Sag Harbor, New York, and pleaded guilty to a reduced charge of non-criminal driving while ability impaired. It's likely that both of these topics will also come up in the documentary.

"I found the whole experience to be really cathartic," Timberlake said. "And I hope that when I do share the things that I share in the documentary, that anybody who's watching it who might have gone through something similar or is just going through anything, can see somebody like myself and sort of feel like, 'Well, if he can have the courage to speak on it and be vulnerable about it' … Maybe I can be a beacon of light for whoever's watching."

Elsewhere during Timberlake's time on "The Tonight Show," he and Fallon revisited their viral 2012 "History of Rap" video by performing a "History of Party Songs," which included "I Want It That Way" by NSYNC's old rivals the Backstreet Boys. Watch the full video below.

articles.title: Comedian Tim Robinson calls police 'dirty pigs' under memorial tribute to killed K-9 officer
articles.summary: Comedian Tim Robinson called Burbank police "dirty pigs" under a memorial video for slain K-9 Spike and accused the department of deleting his comments, which police deny.
articles.body: Comedian Tim Robinson unleashed profane comments against a Southern California police department on Instagram, calling officers "dirty pigs" beneath a tribute to a killed police dog. The "I Think You Should Leave" and "The Chair Company" star left several hostile comments on the Burbank Police Department’s official page earlier this week, attacking officers over a Nov. 22 tribute marking the one-year anniversary of K-9 Spike being shot and killed by an armed suspect after a traffic stop in November 2025. "Dirty pigs made a dog do their violence! Now they celebrate their abuse of an innocent animal? Scum bag pigs," Robinson wrote under the department’s memorial video for the K-9 officer, according to screenshots of the exchange posted online. SHANE GILLIS WISHES EX-GIRLFRIEND 'THE BEST' AFTER TELL-ALL ESSAY ACCUSING HIM OF CHEATING AND 'RED FLAGS' K-9 Spike, a 4-year-old Belgian Malinois, served with the Burbank Police Department for roughly two years and was wearing a ballistic vest when he was killed during a search for an armed suspect who ran from the stop. In additional comments, Robinson argued that Spike never should have been forced into a life-threatening situation and claimed officers chose that fate for him. "F--- you dirty pigs," he wrote, later adding, "Trying to drum up emotion for a dog y’all forced to work. Classic dumb pig s---!" while calling out a specific officer by name. After the remarks disappeared from the post, Robinson returned to the comments section to accuse the department of scrubbing his criticism, writing, "You took my comments down?!!!! What are you trying to hide pigs??!! What about transparency???" A spokesperson for the Burbank Police Department denied removing Robinson’s remarks, telling Fox News Digital, "The Burbank Police Department does not delete comments from its social media posts. However, Instagram has its own policies and procedures that may automatically hide comments identified as derogatory, offensive, or otherwise in violation of the platform’s guidelines." "Additionally, any Instagram user may report a comment they believe violates those guidelines, which may result in Instagram reviewing and hiding the content," the spokesperson added. JIM GAFFIGAN, NEW YORK LAWMAKERS PUSH GOV HOCHUL TO AXE 'UNNECESSARY TAX' HITTING COMEDY CLUBS This latest comment fight is not the first dust-up between the comedian and the Burbank Police Department. In an Oct. 7 post, Robinson and the department went back and forth in the comments, with Robinson calling officers "dirty cops" and "scumbag pigs." The police department initially responded with a crying face emoji, prompting Robinson to reply, "maybe don’t constantly harass and brutalize the community!" From there, the exchange continued with the department telling Robinson it is "open to discussion." He then posted a link to a FOX 11 Los Angeles report in which Aerin Robinson accused the Burbank Police Department of police brutality after his October 2025 arrest. The arrest, captured on body camera video, showed a man with a bloodied face being struck with a stun gun. Aerin Robinson was initially stopped for suspected drug possession and resisting arrest. The case was dismissed by a judge after the preliminary hearing, according to the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office. As the comments continued under the post, Tim Robinson asked the police department why it would not comment on the case, to which the department responded, "We’re aware of the allegations. We don’t comment on pending litigation." The department also added, "I encourage you to learn about why we have oleoresin capsicum aka OC as a force option to use." COMEDIAN ALFRED ROBLES WEARS MANY HATS: COWBOY, CATHOLIC AND CROWD THERAPIST The comedian continued to suggest that the department consistently used unnecessary force and lacked patience, adding, "it’s hard to keep track of cuz yall got a lot of beating allegations." articles.title: Why Advent calendars are thriving in the ‘little treat’ economy
articles.summary: Creators on TikTok and Instagram are helping to fuel the advent calendar craze, one review video at a time.
articles.body: The countdown to Christmas began in October — at least on social media. Over the past few months, content creators have been getting a head start on the holidays by unboxing, reviewing and promoting an array of Advent calendars. The anticipation behind each cardboard flap has translated into millions of views, as consumers lean into the surge in popularity surrounding the product. “Brands are bringing out their advent calendars earlier and earlier, and so they go faster every year,” said TikTok creator Courtney Cahoon, who said nowadays she’s purchasing the calendars as early as August and sharing highlights with her 1.7 million followers. The calendars originated in Germany in the 20th century, where a printer took inspiration from the candies attached to cardboard he had used to count down to Christmas as a child, according to retail giant Williams Sonoma. While the calendars are not a new holiday offering, demand for the product has increased in recent years — which explains why it might feel like there’s a calendar for just about everything and for just about everyone. Global market for such calendars could reach $2.47 billion by 2033, according to trade publication Retail Insider. Nowadays, the calendars have evolved into a marketing vehicle for brands looking to showcase everything from everyday essentials like McCormick’s spices to luxury goods like a $1,020 set of mini perfumes from Maison Francis Kurkdijan. Experts like Freddy Tran Nager, an associate professor of communication at the University of Southern California, attribute the popularity of the calendars to what’s called “the treat economy.” “We’ve had a rough few years,” said Nager, the founder of the marketing consultancy Atomic Tango LLC, referring to the economic challenges facing the U.S. economy. “And so you know, some people indulge in what’s called the ‘treat economy.’ They can’t afford a car. They can’t afford a home, but they can certainly afford little treats for themselves.” Creators who specialize in sharing product recommendations on their feeds — sometimes in exchange for a commission from the brands — have also encouraged users to lean into indulging in calendar deals earlier and earlier. On platforms like TikTok, searches for “advent calendar” spiked from Nov. 2-8, with the app reporting that many of its creators have posted videos sharing which calendars are underrated and which offer the best value. Ahead of Black Friday, TikTok said in a recent weekly trends report that more “creators are sharing holiday gift guides and reviewing advent calendars. Shoppers are also turning to TikTok Shop for holiday finds.” Faire, an online wholesale platform that tracks consumer habits, told NBC News in an email that “by the end of September, retailers had already spent more on advent calendars than in all of last season.” Hannah Wall, Faire’s trend expert, also attributed to the popularity of the advent calendar to “treat culture,” citing peak interest from Gen Z. “Gen Z has made it an adult staple because it’s the ultimate small treat and they’re choosing squishies, tea, jam, and beauty countdowns over chocolate for a daily dose of holiday joy,” Wall wrote in an email statement. Jintao Zhang, an assistant professor of marketing at Binghamton University, offered a similar observation. “We know that the largest consumer group consuming social media is Gen Z,” he said, adding that the age group “determines the prevalence and also the attractiveness of advent calendar on social media.” Social media users also tend to trust content creators, particularly those with smaller followings who are known as “micro” or “nano” influencers, according to Zhang. Still, he warned people to be cautious as some influencers post content that is sponsored without necessarily disclosing it in an obvious way. Influencers typically approach their calendar videos in two different ways: Some do countdowns, going through each day of the calendar individually (as intended); while others open an entire calendar in one video, sharing its contents altogether. Natalie Violette, a beauty and lifestyle influencer with more than 4 million followers on TikTok, said she either purchases or receives the calendars from brands in an effort to maintain authenticity in her reviews. “They like seeing … the honest reactions and reviews on these calendars, and definitely … the surprise factor, no question, I think that’s what really brings them in,” said Violette, whose journey with this type of content began three years ago when a follower challenged her to do a complete makeup look just by using products from a calendar. Her calendar videos have become so popular that they draw in new viewers every holiday season. The calendars she posts often sell out, she added. Even calendars that she isn’t a fan of pick up traction online. For example, Violette was among the creators who criticized the Skims calendar, which, for $148, included hair ties and bobby pins. As a result of the online backlash, the Kim Kardashian-owned brand began offering refunds to customers who were unhappy with the product. Sarah Lynn, who has built a following of more than 200,000 followers on TikTok for her calendar content, described it as “super fun” to show people what’s on the market. Sometimes, however, she said the offerings are hit or miss. She particularly doesn’t appreciate when brands are “just filling it with random kinds of junk that they know are not really their best selling products.” “If this was not my job and if this wasn’t what I was doing for work, I would not be spending all this money,” Lynn said. “But I never want people to feel like they have to buy anything or that they’re necessarily missing out.” “Whatever people want to take from my content, they can definitely take from it,” she added. “Whether it’s entertainment or shopping inspiration or neither.”

articles.title: Quote of the day by Patrick Stewart: ‘My dream became more of a dream,’ the 'X-Men' star on finding purpose and following your passion
articles.summary: Discover Patrick Stewart's transformative path from a challenging childhood in Yorkshire to becoming a beloved actor in 'X-Men' and 'Star Trek'. Explore his insights on passion, purpose, and the impact of encouragement.
articles.body: We've all pictured what life might look like if things were different. A career you've always wanted, a place you'd love to live, or just a way out of circumstances that make you miserable. But actually believing a different future is possible can take a while. For Sir Patrick Stewart, that realisation hit when he was a young boy in Yorkshire, long before he became one of the most recognisable faces in Hollywood.The late actor, best known as Professor Charles Xavier in ‘X-Men’ and Captain Jean-Luc Picard in ‘Star Trek’, had a childhood that looked nothing like the career he built. He grew up in a working-class family and found comfort in books, then discovered acting through a schoolteacher. Years later, he recalled how performing on stage made him realise the life he'd only imagined could become real.Today's quote of the day by Patrick Stewart reads: “I escaped. And my dream became more of a dream. Not just of having a different life. But, for the few minutes I had on stage, actually living it.”He said it to journalist Alex Moshakis for ‘The Observer’, published through The Guardian on October 1, 2023. Talking about his memoir, ‘Making It So’, he described growing up in Mirfield and how his English teacher, Cecil Dormand, introduced him to Shakespeare. Stewart remembered struggling with the language of ‘The Merchant of Venice,’ but once he started performing, he felt a sense of escape from his difficult home life.What does the quote by Patrick Stewart mean?It's about the moment something you've only imagined starts to feel possible. As a kid Sir Patrick Stewart wanted a different life, but he didn't necessarily know what that would look like or how to get there.Acting gave him a taste of something beyond the world he knew. For a few minutes on stage he could be someone else and forget what was happening at home.What stands out is that he wasn't talking about fame or becoming a successful actor. He was remembering what it felt like to find something that genuinely excited him, and that gave him a reason to picture a future different from his present. Finding something you love can change what you believe you're capable of.How is the quote by Patrick Stewart relevant today?It's easy to write off your dreams when they feel miles away from where you are now. Maybe you want to work in a creative field, switch careers or try something you've never had the nerve for.To quote Sir Patrick Stewart, you don't have to know everything before you get curious about something. Sometimes trying it for the first time is what shows you how much it matters.His story also shows the power of encouragement. Stewart had teachers who saw something in him and opened doors he may never have walked through on his own. That kind of support is revolutionary when you're just trying to believe in yourself.Patrick Stewart's early yearsPatrick Stewart was born in Mirfield, West Yorkshire, England, on 13 July 1940 into a working-class family and was subjected to domestic abuse as a child. His father, Alfred Stewart, had served in the military, and his mother, Gladys, worked in a textile mill.Books and cinema became his escapes. At school, Cecil Dormand pushed him toward Shakespeare and acting. Stewart later won a scholarship to Bristol Old Vic Theatre School, which gave him the chance to train professionally.How did Patrick Stewart rise to fame?Sir Patrick Stewart started out in British repertory theatre before joining the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966, and spent years on classical plays, building a reputation as a stage actor.The international breakthrough came in 1987, when he was cast as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in ‘Star Trek: The Next Generation’. A whole other generation of fans met him as Professor Charles Xavier in the ‘X-Men’ films, starting in 2000. He kept working across theatre, television and cinema throughout his career. He passed away on October 28, 2026, at the age of 86.Looking back at that 2023 interview, his words land a bit differently now. A young boy who dreamed of escaping his circumstances went on to spend his life bringing characters to the stage and screen. And it all began with a teacher who handed him Shakespeare and let him find out what acting could do.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI is a different kind of GTA — so it needed a different kind of ending
articles.summary: GTA 6 producer Rob Nelson explains Rockstar’s approach to the ending and post-game of the new open-world game.
articles.body: In most Grand Theft Auto games, and most open-world games for that matter, the world is left open for you to explore once the credits roll. It could be Los Santos or a twisted take on Manhattan, but the idea is that the main story is just one part of the experience. After that’s done, there are usually still places you haven’t explored or side missions you left lingering. But Grand Theft Auto VI doesn’t work quite the same way. Because of its storyline, which involves a couple trying to get out of the criminal life for good, that kind of ending didn’t really fit. “In this one it didn’t make sense,” Rob Nelson, producer on GTA VI and co-studio head at developer Rockstar North, told me ahead of the game’s launch. “Their story needed to end and have some kind of conclusion.” This story contains light spoilers for the ending of Grand Theft Auto VI, along with a key plot point from chapter 1. To be clear, you can still play GTA VI after the main storyline wraps up. But in order for that to happen, you have to zip back in time to a moment before a pivotal decision — I won’t spoil it for you — that alters the lives of main characters Jason and Lucia, along with their young son Tomás, who they’re attempting to get custody of. Nelson says the team tried “all sorts of things” but soon realized that “in no way did it make sense” to have the game end like a traditional GTA experience. “You go back and have this open time again where you have the best single-player safehouse you’ve ever had in a GTA, with a garage full of supercars, a helipad, a gym, and all of the stuff you could ever want,” he says of the solution the studio landed on. “And you can spend as long as you want there. But you don’t have Tommy. So the characters don’t have the one thing that they wanted at the start. There’s the tension where you have to spend some extra time grinding to make some more money without knowing what it’s going to get you, and it plays out differently if you get that money.” One advantage of this structure is that it lets you try out different endings. GTA VI’s story can wrap up in multiple ways based on a variety of factors: how much money you have saved up, what kind of criminal you were throughout the game, and some key decisions you’re forced to make in the final moments. The new postgame structure creates an opportunity to see some of the alternate ways the story can go. “There’s a large number of potential outcomes based on how you played it,” Nelson says.

articles.title: Dec Donnelly says I'm a Celebrity tension 'became much bigger deal than it should have'
articles.summary: The co-hosts discussed tensions that flared between Mariella Frostrup and AJ Odudu on the show.
articles.body:
I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here host Declan Donnelly has said tensions between Mariella Frostrup and AJ Odudu over cooking duties on the show "became a much bigger deal than it should have".

Co-host Ant McPartlin said "cooking makes things very tense in camp", adding: "If they could zoom out a little bit in there, they'll realise it's not that deep. But they just can't, once they're in there".

Donnelly and McPartlin discussed on their podcast how relations became fractious, when Odudu attempted to help Frostrup cook on Saturday's episode - the next day Odudu was distressed after Frostrup accused her of being "aggressive".

On Wednesday 887 people complained to Ofcom about Sunday's episode in relation to "alleged bullying behaviour" by Frostrup towards Odudu.

Frostrup apologised during an amicable conversation on Tuesday, and Odudu accepted, explaining it was "triggering" because "it's a strong word to use in casual scenarios, particularly towards black women".

On their podcast, Hanging Out with Ant and Dec, Donnelly said tensions in camp started "surprisingly early".

"From day one cooking was tense and then it obviously came to a head with AJ and Mariella, and it spilled over to breakfast the next morning," he said.

McPartlin added: "You have 12 hungry mouths to feed and you and your sous chef, the other chef, are cooking and everyone is stood around looking at them. The pressure is quite a lot."

Donnelly continued: "When you are there, and so much of your life revolves around that mealtime, it's the only meal of the day you really get that isn't rice and beans.

"There is a lot of pressure and obviously Mariella was feeling that pressure.

"AJ wanted to come in and help and it all came to a head, and maybe because there was so much pressure and because it was so important, Mariella maybe didn't handle it very well around the campfire when she was cooking, and it spilled over into the next day - and it became a much bigger deal than it should have done."

He said the "most important thing" was that "the two ladies were able to sit down and drew a line under it, they were adult enough to sit there, talk it through, and move on together. If more people did that the world would be a much better place".

McPartlin agreed, saying: "If some of our leaders did that, the world would be a better place."

On Wednesday, an Ofcom spokesperson told BBC News: "We are assessing the complaints against our rules, but are yet to decide whether or not to investigate."

On Thursday night, Frostrup completed her fourth bushtucker trial, which is voted for by the public.

Many viewers defended Odudu after the encounter.

They included broadcaster and comic Judi Love who said she felt "triggered by Frostrup's comment, while Britain's Got Talent judge and Strictly Come Dancing judge Motsi Mabuse also gave their support to Odudu.

BBC Radio 1 DJ Clara Amfo said: "Calling a black woman 'aggressive' when she is being anything else but is a classic microaggression."

Speaking on spin-off show I'm A Celebrity... Unpacked on Sunday, former campmate Jordan Banjo said Frostrup had handled the situation "poorly", but urged people to "give a bit of grace to Mariella, and everyone in the camp" because "you can't judge an abnormal situation by normal standards".

It is "a really weird situation that every single person's in, and I'm not sure if people go at stuff with the clearest head", he said, explaining: "You get these weird breakdowns, and I think that's what we're seeing."

An ITV statement said: "The production monitors everyone in camp 24/7 and if at any time we feel someone has overstepped the line by using inappropriate language or displaying unacceptable behaviour, we would take steps to intervene and speak to everyone involved.

"The duty of care for our contestants is of the utmost importance to us. We take the welfare of the celebrities very seriously and have measures in place to ensure they are supported at every stage of the process: before, during and after filming."

articles.title: Netflix Edits Schizophrenia Scene Out Of Tyson Fury Doc After Wife Reveals Boxer Does Not Have Condition
articles.summary: Tyson Fury does not have schizophrenia and a scene in which his wife claims he does has been edited out of the Netflix movie about the British boxing superst...
articles.body:
Tyson Fury does not have schizophrenia and a scene in which his wife claims he does has been edited out of the Netflix movie about the British boxing superstar.

The doc, titled Tyson Fury, provides a tell-all account of Fury's mental health struggles as he builds up to his fight with Anthony Joshua next month, which is also on Netflix.

The trailer initially showed Fury's wife Paris Fury saying the boxer is a "mild schizophrenic," but amid questions from the boxing regulator, this has now been revealed to be untrue.

"I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary," a statement from Paris Fury said. "I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson's condition and I used the word 'schizophrenic.' While Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn't have this condition and has never received a diagnosis."

A Netflix spokeswoman said the scene has been removed from the doc, which dropped today.

"Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson's official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch," she added.

Following the schizophrenia comments, which were also included in a Netflix press release about the doc on Monday, the British Boxing Board of Control said it had been examining whether what was thought to be Fury's diagnosis would get in the way of his long-anticipated fight with fellow British boxer Joshua.

That fight has now been cleared to take place on December 11 in Cardiff and could prove to be one of Netflix's most lucrative live sporting events.

Fury's doc is billed as a "raw, real, unfiltered" look at "the man behind the boxing icon." Fury has also appeared in two seasons of Netflix's ob-doc At Home With the Furys, with a third in motion. Both the feature doc and TV show are produced by Banijay-backed Optomen.

The comedy legend once tried to quit his hit CBS sitcom, "The Bob Newhart Show," only to discover the network wasn't ready to let its ratings star walk away. The contract dispute is detailed in Michael Seth Starr's biography, "Bob Newhart: The Life and Laughter of an American Treasure," which chronicles the comedian's nearly 65-year career. BOB NEWHART, LEGENDARY COMEDIAN AND SITCOM STAR, DEAD AT 94 Newhart wasn't exactly in a position to face a multimillion-dollar lawsuit. "I don't have $6 million," the comedian later admitted. "And my wife wouldn't lend me any of her money." Although he publicly credited fan support for his decision, Newhart later acknowledged that financial pressure played a major role in his return. "When I said I wanted to quit, the people in the cast and the production crew were all affected, of course and they helped influence me to change my mind. Then there were letters from fans and people I met on the street. But I guess the main reason I decided to come back was that CBS threatened to sue me for $6 million because there was a year left on my contract." According to Starr's biography, Newhart approached CBS executives Bob Daly and Robert Wussler about leaving "The Bob Newhart Show" before its sixth season. His attorney warned that if a replacement series failed to generate comparable revenue, CBS could seek damages Newhart estimated at "about fifty or sixty million dollars." The comedian also questioned the show's creative future, with head writers Tom Patchett and Jay Tarses occupied with other projects. "So, I thought maybe five years was enough. I'd rather go off a year early than a year late," he recalled. He hoped to negotiate television specials instead, saying, "I'd rather do specials, even if it means walking away from a lot of money." CBS ultimately convinced him to return for a sixth and final season, with Starr describing concessions that included better scripts, flexibility to miss one or two episodes and "a modest bump" in his $30,000-per-episode salary. articles.title: El duro reproche de Silvia Intxaurrondo a Feijóo tras no ir a su entrevista: "Nosotros sí hemos hecho nuestro trabajo"
articles.standfirst: El programa mostró la silla vacía que tenían reservada para él en la televisión pública
articles.summary: El programa mostró la silla vacía que tenían reservada para él en la televisión pública
articles.body: La presentadora de La Hora de La 1, Silvia Intxaurrondo, ha protagonizado este viernes una contundente intervención en directo tras la ausencia del candidato del Partido Popular a la presidencia del Gobierno, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, quien tenía agendada una entrevista en la cadena pública que finalmente no se ha producido. Al arranque de la franja prevista para el encuentro, la periodista ha querido explicar a la audiencia los pormenores de lo ocurrido. "Son las 9:02, 8:02 en Canarias, en torno a esta hora tendríamos que estar entrevistando en este programa al candidato del Partido Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo. Él tenía 30 minutos reservados en este programa según el plan de cobertura de Radio Televisión Española y el tiempo asignado por la Junta Electoral Central", ha comenzado señalando Intxaurrondo. Según el relato de la comunicadora, el equipo del líder popular había trasladado previamente a los medios de comunicación su intención de participar en el espacio televisivo, aunque la confirmación oficial hacia la propia cadena nunca llegaba. "Hace días el Partido Popular, Núñez Feijóo confirmó a la prensa que iba a venir, pero curiosamente a quienes teníamos que realizar esta entrevista no nos lo confirmaba y anoche a escasas horas de esta entrevista hoy nos decía que si finalmente se celebraba nos iban a avisar con antelación. Y fíjense que eso que conocían el plan de cobertura desde hacía más de tres semanas, ¿no?", ha detallado en antena. Intxaurrondo ha subrayado la desigualdad de condiciones entre la obligación de servicio público de la corporación y la decisión unilateral de la formación política. "Y aquí hay una asimetría que nosotros queremos explicar. Ellos tienen libertad de venir o de no venir. Pero nosotros tenemos la obligación de garantizarles ese espacio. ¿Y eso qué significa? Eso significa preparar una entrevista, organizar a todo un equipo y poner a su disposición recursos públicos", ha recalcado. Pese a reconocer la potestad del candidato para declinar la invitación, la periodista ha censurado las formas empleadas por el Partido Popular durante las horas previas. "Por supuesto que el señor Feijóo tiene derecho a no venir, lo que nos parece muy cuestionable es la forma de proceder por una cuestión de seriedad, de compromiso institucional y de respeto al trabajo de los demás. Y desde luego esta forma de proceder suscita dudas sobre la buena fe con la que se ha procedido. No era tan difícil decir que no iba a venir porque nosotros sí hemos hecho nuestro trabajo. La entrevista está preparada y las preguntas también. Pero el señor Feijóo no se ha presentado", ha lamentado. En el tramo final de su exposición, la presentadora ha elevado el tono para denunciar la contradicción entre los anuncios previos del partido y la realidad del plantón, vinculándolo con las críticas vertidas desde la formación hacia los profesionales de la casa. "El señor Feijóo que se presenta como un hombre de palabra mintió a los periodistas cuando hace exactamente una semana dijo que sí, que sí que iba a venir a este programa a ser entrevistado. ¿Saben qué hay peor que les mientan a ustedes diciendo que somos comisarios políticos? Que no sean capaces de venir y decirlo mirándonos a los ojos. No sea qué les vayamos a contestar", ha afirmado. Para concluir, Intxaurrondo ha recordado que diversos medios digitales y escritos publicaron días atrás la asistencia del político tras las filtraciones de su propio equipo de comunicación, dejando en evidencia a los redactores que cubren la información del partido. "El Partido Popular mintió a todos esos compañeros. Compañeros que alucinaron cuando me llamaron, me escribieron, y yo decía: 'Pues os lo habrá confirmado a vosotros, pero a mí no'. A toda traía en titular: 'Iba a venir'. Es imposible que venga. Ha elegido por lo que sea estar en otro sitio sin decirnos a nosotros que no iba a venir y mintiendo a la prensa de este país con la boca así de grande", ha sentenciado antes de dar paso a la tertulia.

articles.body: Katy Perry and Justin Trudeau took luxury travel to another level during their European holiday, travelling from Paris to Venice aboard an Orient Express carriage reportedly costing £80,000 a night. The couple had an entire private carriage to themselves, complete with a golden bathtub, a library containing 1,000 books, a personal butler and an elaborate dining area.The singer offered glimpses of the journey, including a relaxing soak in a golden bath before changing into a champagne-coloured satin minidress for dinner. Her boyfriend, the former Canadian prime minister, opted for a white tuxedo with black trousers and a bow tie as they enjoyed cocktails and a private evening aboard the train.The couple also played cards in an ornate dining carriage featuring a large gold lamp. But it was the extraordinary accommodation, rather than just the journey itself, that made their Orient Express experience particularly exclusive.Inside L'Observatoire, the private Orient Express carriageAccording to the Daily Mail, Katy Perry and Justin Trudeau stayed in L'Observatoire, a private carriage added to the train last year. Designed as an exclusive retreat, it features a double bedroom, a dining area and a library stocked with 1,000 books.The carriage also has skylights fitted with windscreen wipers to keep them clear during rainy weather. The couple had access to a personal butler who attended to their requirements, including preparing Katy Perry's bath. An abundant supply of caviar and champagne was also part of the experience.One particularly unusual detail concerns the golden bathtub. The train reportedly does not slow down while a passenger is bathing, preventing the water from splashing. The feature is said to be a luxury previously enjoyed by British monarchs travelling on the royal train.The couple's privacy was another significant aspect of the arrangement. Their carriage was positioned at the end of the train, making it unlikely that they would encounter other passengers during the journey.Katy Perry's dinner look and arrival in VeniceFor dinner aboard the train, Katy Perry wore a champagne-coloured satin minidress by De La Vali, reportedly priced at £660. articles.body: Craig Morgan and his family spend their winters off the grid in Alaska, where their nearest neighbor is seven miles away. "We go up after Christmas and we like to try to stay till March," the country singer told Fox News Digital. "Now, sometimes we'll leave and come back home, depending if I have something to do — If I have a show or a speaking engagement or anything like that.
